answer_1.quote: Dialog tutoring systems aim to tutor students by holding a conversation with them. Formally, the goal of dialog tutoring is to continue a tutoring dialog consisting of a sequence of T -1 turns H := (u 1 , . . . , u T -1 ) taken by either student or teacher. ... Continuation then means generating a new utterance u T ∈ V * .

answer_2.quote: We report standard text generation metrics: the sacrebleu implementation of BLEU (sBLEU) to measure word overlap and BERTScore (BF1, using the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 checkpoint) to measure semantic similarity. Moreover, we report the knowledge F1 (KF1) score with respect to the grounding information...

answer_3.quote: we also prompt LLAMA3-70B and use it complementary to human evaluation... to assess how targeted, correct, and actionable a response is.

answer_4.quote: We conduct a human evaluation using teachers as expert annotators... We assess whether the generated responses are targeted, correct, and actionable without outright telling the solution.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluated on targetedness, correctness, and actionability of the tutor responses
